note: A second, deliberately harder set, separate from semantic_cases so that neither set's figures are reported as the other's. Every case declares a reading_status, and renderings are grouped under the reading they express, so two wordings of one reading are distinguishable from two admissible readings. Documents and spans are written to be scorable by the same anchoring and meaning machinery as the first set.

reading_statuses.determinate: the span settles one reading; a projection that picks any other is wrong
reading_statuses.ambiguous: the span admits several readings and does not decide between them; a projection that silently commits to one has added information
reading_statuses.underdetermined_quantifier: the span leaves a plural open, so both the universal resolution and the explicit non-universal one add a commitment the source does not make
reading_statuses.evidence_absent: the span asserts something the document does not support; the projection must still render the assertion, and must not soften it into a hedge

requirement_types.readings: each entry is one reading, with every rendering that expresses it; a determinate case has one, an ambiguous case has at least two
requirement_types.requires_all_groups: each group is an OR over acceptable renderings; one claim on the span must satisfy every group
requirement_types.forbids: regexes that must not match a claim's canonical_content
requirement_types.forbidden_readings: example propositions that would be meaning errors here
requirement_types.min_claims_on_span: how many distinct claims the span must carry
